messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up on ingress -> proxy -> runtime handoff for streaming. We've been hit by two failure classes in the wild: early client aborts and midstream runtime restarts. Need a clear lifecycle model + minimal surface changes for runtimes. Thoughts?

tim: Can we keep the model small: RESERVED -> STREAMING -> HANDOFF -> RESUMABLE | TERMINATED. Handshake only needs a tiny header exchange. :thinking_face:

sasha: I prefer opaque resume tokens issued by the edge rather than sticky session affinity. Token should encode checkpoint pointer + model version. Keeps edge mostly stateless. Tradeoff: token size vs security/attestation.

raj: Token is fine, but for endpoints that produce side-effects we need duplicate suppression. Recommend mandating idempotency-key semantics at the application layer for any resumeable path that can trigger external effects.

maria: Agreed. Also practical concern: resume latency. If resuming requires replaying a huge prefix into runtime, clients will see big spikes. Proposal: incremental checkpoints every N tokens + KV store with TTL.

tim: Ops cost question: storing checkpoints for many in-flight streams can explode memory. Suggest store deltas, compress, and auto-downgrade to non-resumable after configured quota per tenant. Also expose policy: resumable=false if checkpoint size > X.

sasha: @maria can you sketch the handshake headers? Something like X-Resume-Token and X-Stream-Checkpoint and a 409 when model versions are incompatible.

maria: Sketch of the header flow: 
```
Client -> Edge: POST /v1/stream
  - X-Client-Id: abc
Edge -> Runtime: POST /internal/stream
  - X-Stream-Mode: proxied
Runtime -> Edge (ack): 200 + X-Resume-Token: <opaque-token>
Client -> Edge (resume): POST /v1/stream
  - X-Resume-Token: <opaque-token>
Edge -> Runtime (resume): POST /internal/stream/resume
  - X-Resume-Token: <opaque-token>
Runtime -> Edge: 200 or 409 (incompatible model/version)
```

deploy-bot: deployed rfc/edge-resume-probe v0.1 — https://ci.internal/runs/4523 :rocket:

maria: Proposed firm decisions for the follow-up RFC: (1) edge issues opaque resume tokens, (2) runtime must accept resume tokens and perform a version check, returning 409 on mismatch, (3) default token TTL 30m, tenant-configurable, (4) edge falls back to non-resumable behavior if runtime doesn't support resume.

raj: Add the following metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fallback_rate, resume_avg_replay_tokens, resume_token_issued_count. Those feed alerts for regressions.

sasha: Backwards compatibility note: older runtimes will simply ignore X-Resume-Token headers. Edge should detect that and downgrade gracefully (metric + non-resumable response) rather than surfacing a 5xx to clients.

tim: Fallback plan: if runtime ignores resume token, edge treats the stream as non-resumable, emits resume_unsupported metric, and serves the request normally. Avoid returning 5xx to upstream clients.

maria: I'll open the RFC PR with sequence diagrams, perf probe checklist (load test resume w/ checkpoint sizes of 1k/10k/100k tokens), and an ops playbook for token TTL tuning. Ping for review before Wed arch sync. :pray:
